devotionals.text: “And if ye call on the Father, who without respect of persons judgeth according to every man's work, pass the time of your sojourning here in fear.” – 1 Peter 1:17.
devotionals.comment: In his first epistle to the “strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, Peter an Apostle of Jesus Christ, charged them to holiness, in all manner of conversation, reminding them, and by extension, Christian converts in general, that their redemption was effected by means of Christ's shed blood, and not with things corruptible, for which reason, they should aspire for holiness, as God who has called us is holy. In verse 17, he charges us to live in the fear of God, which Solomon designates “the whole duty of man.” (Ecclesiastes 12:13) Taking a cue from the “heroes and heroines of faith”, Paul the Apostle eulogised their uncommon faith in God Almighty in looking forward to inheriting “a better country: for which they considered themselves “strangers and pilgrims on the earth.” (Hebrews 11:13-16) On our part, as we march on to the antitypical Canaan, “It is good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from this withdraw not thine hand: for he that feareth God shall come forth of them all.” – Ecclesiastes 7:18.

devotionals.theme: STEDFASTNESS IN GOD'S SERVICE
devotionals.text: “For then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear.” – Job 11:15.
devotionals.comment: To be steadfast means to be resolutely or dutifully firm and unwavering. In our service to God, it means the worshipper has a conviction and is firm on the decision to serve God faithfully till the end, trusting without doubt the sure promises of God in this world and most importantly in God's Kingdom. There are many hindrances to one's steadfastness. One of such is sin in whatever form. We need therefore to be circumspect always in our lives. We are not perfect, but we strive for it. In doing so, we would be steadfast by God's grace. “Canst thou by searching find out God? canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection? If thou prepare thine heart, and stretch out thine hands toward him; If iniquity be in thine hand, put it far away, and let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacles.” – Job 11:7,13,14.

devotionals.theme: STEDFASTNESS IN GOD'S SERVICE
devotionals.text: “And might not be as their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation; a generation that set not their heart aright, and whose spirit was not stedfast with God.” – Psalms 78:8.
devotionals.comment: The history of the Jews in the Holy Bible is plagued with stories of lack of steadfastness due to stubbornness and rebellious spirit. God Almighty told Moses “…I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people:” (Deuteronomy 9:13) Their stubbornness and recalcitrant attitude did not favour them. It brought on them the anger of God and many of them where destroyed or taken captive. Their stories are written for our learning and admonition. To avoid this therefore, we must set our hearts to obey God. The Holy Scriptures admonished us: “Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked. For the LORD your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, a mighty, and a terrible, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward.” – Deuteronomy 10:16,17.

devotionals.theme: STEDFASTNESS IN GOD'S SERVICE
devotionals.text: “For their heart was not right with him, neither were they stedfast in his covenant.” – Psalms 78:37.
devotionals.comment: The intent of the heart affects our service to God. The thoughts of the heart are open to God. “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.” (Hebrews 4:13) The covenant God Almighty had with the Jews was obedience which will earn them His blessings, prosperity and progress. He spoke through Jeremiah the prophet in Jeremiah 7:22,23: “For I spake not unto your fathers, nor commanded them in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.”

devotionals.theme: STEDFASTNESS IN GOD'S SERVICE
devotionals.text: “And they continued stedfastly in the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.” – Acts 2:42.
devotionals.comment: On the day of Pentecost, the apostles received the anointing of the Holy Spirit and spoke in tongues. They spoke in languages people heard and understood. (Acts 2:1-11) Apostle Peter spoke about repentance to those whose consciences were pricked by the word of God. (Acts 2:37-39) It is further stated “And with many other words did he testify and exhort, saying, Save yourselves from this untoward generation.” (Acts 2:40) Then “... they that gladly received his word were baptized: and the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls.” (Acts 2:41) These are they which continued steadfastly to what was preached to them. Being therefore an example and encouragement to us to do so in our service to God for our own blessings and salvation at the end.

devotionals.theme: STEDFASTNESS IN GOD'S SERVICE
devotionals.text: “Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.” – 1 Corinthians 15:58.
devotionals.comment: The Bible states “God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?” (Numbers 23:19) We labour in the service of God in various ways. We do so by our time, physical presence, financial support for the work of God, resisting sin, helping others etc. Those who are doing these therefore should not allow anything to truncate their resolve to continue to do God's work. Instead, efforts should be made to do more and even diversify our works by God's grace. “Know therefore that the LORD thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations.” – Deuteronomy 7:9.

devotionals.theme: STEDFASTNESS IN GOD'S SERVICE
devotionals.text: “For though I be absent in the flesh, yet am I with you in the spirit, joying and beholding your order, and the stedfastness of your faith in Christ.” – Colossians 2:5.
devotionals.comment: Apostle Paul with the spirit of God in him was able to account for and commend the steadfastness of the Christians at Colosse. As it was at that time, so it is now. There are people who are used by the devil to try to persuade us out of our righteousness, belief in true doctrines and steadfastness. St Paul therefore warned in Colossians 2:6,8: “As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him: Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men, after the rudiments of the world, and not after Christ.” To Timothy, St. Paul wrote: “Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils.” – 1 Timothy 4:1.

devotionals.theme: STEDFASTNESS IN GOD'S SERVICE
devotionals.text: “For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end.” – Hebrews 3:14.
devotionals.comment: For one to serve God, there is a confidence in Him and His word. This assurance at heart can be affected by various trials, tribulations and temptations at the instance of the Devil resulting from our service to God. It can also be affected by evil counsel from anyone against our knowledge and faith. King Solomon says: “My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not.” See also 1 Corinthians 15:33. The Bible exhorts: “Cast not away therefore your confidence, which hath great recompence of reward. For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise. Now the just shall live by faith: but if any man draw back, my soul shall have no pleasure in him. But we are not of them who draw back unto perdition; but of them that believe to the saving of the soul.” – Hebrews 10:35,36,38,39.

devotionals.theme: STEDFASTNESS IN GOD'S SERVICE
devotionals.text: “And our hope of you is stedfast, knowing, that as ye are partakers of the sufferings, so shall ye be also of the consolation.” – 2 Corinthians 1:7.
devotionals.comment: It is common knowledge that some persons who are active in God's work do experience terrible things at the instance of the devil. St. Paul here is stating that such ones will be rewarded by God Almighty in this life and most importantly in God's kingdom when it is fully established. We are admonished: "Whom resist stedfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world. But the God of all grace, who hath called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you. To him be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen." (1 Peter 5 :9-11) We should therefore be steadfast in our service to God for our own blessings and salvation.

devotionals.theme: STEDFASTNESS IN GOD'S SERVICE
devotionals.text: “Ye therefore, beloved, seeing ye know these things before, beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness.” – 2 Peter 3:17.
devotionals.comment: The knowledge of the word of God is very important. It is a shield against the wiles of the devil. “For wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence: but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom giveth life to them that have it.” (Ecclesiastes 7:12) With wisdom and the help of God, we are able to be firm in our steadfastness. That is understanding. King David prayed: “Give me understanding, and I shall keep thy law; yea, I shall observe it with my whole heart. Make me to go in the path of thy commandments; for therein do I delight...Thou art my portion, O LORD: I have said that I would keep thy words." (Psalms 119:34,35,57) St. Peter said: “But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ....” – 2 Peter 3:18.

devotionals.theme: STEDFASTNESS IN GOD'S SERVICE
devotionals.text: “And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many.” – Matthew 24:11.
devotionals.comment:
God does not do miracles through humans anymore. We should learn from the story in Acts 8:9-11. “But there was a certain man, called Simon, which beforetime in the same city used sorcery, and bewitched the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one: To whom they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is the great power of God. And to him they had regard, because that of long time he had bewitched them with sorceries." Christ warned “For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect. Behold, I have told you before.” (Matthew 24:24,25) Some in pursuits of miracles and healing have fallen away from the true Faith. This is at the instance of the devil who is using these false prophets to lure as many persons as possible to destruction.

We should beware and be steadfast by God's grace.

devotionals.theme: STEDFASTNESS IN GOD'S SERVICE
devotionals.text: “For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica…” – 2 Timothy 4:10.
devotionals.comment: The glamour and excitement of the pleasures apparently seen in the world has seduced some away from their steadfastness to God. This unfortunately fulfilled on Demas as seen in the text for today. The Bible warns us against the cares of this life in 1 John 2:15-17 to wit: “Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him. For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world. And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.” No matter the extent of pleasure, apparent fame, wealth and so on, it all amounts to vanity at the end. – Ecclesiastes 1:2,3.

devotionals.theme: STEDFASTNESS IN GOD'S SERVICE
devotionals.text: “So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.” – Hebrews 3:19.
devotionals.comment: Unbelief is an absence of faith. Any unfavourable circumstance can cause unbelief in one who is not spiritually minded. When one lacks faith under such circumstances, it will affect one's steadfastness and for some, falling away entirely from the service of God. We should guide our faith jealously with knowledge and prayers at all times. Lack of faith also makes one to commit sin. Many of the Jews did not get to the promised land because of unbelief. St Paul warned: “Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it. For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.” – Hebrews 4:1,2.

devotionals.theme: STEDFASTNESS IN GOD'S SERVICE
devotionals.text: “This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men.” – Titus 3:8.
devotionals.comment: One of the factors that have been seen to affect steadfastness is the notion that “I have done enough, let others do it”. As long as we are still alive we are expected to keep on whatever good works we are doing by God's grace. St Paul said in Philippians 3:13-15 “Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus. Let us therefore, as many as be perfect, be thus minded: and if in any thing ye be otherwise minded, God shall reveal even this unto you." “But it is good to be zealously affected always in a good thing, and not only when I am present with you.” – Galatians 4:18.

devotionals.theme: STEDFASTNESS IN GOD'S SERVICE
devotionals.text: “Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.” – Philippians 2:12.
devotionals.comment:
In the service to our Maker, it is true we help one another, but we should not allow anyone to affect our steadfastness to God and His service. Dedication to others' welfare has affected the steadfastness of some negatively. Importantly also, eye service is not profitable. Some are pretentious. Only when they are in the view of certain persons such as the leaders, rulers, or those in authority, that they become zealous. The Holy Bible says: “...not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God: And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men;

Knowing that of the Lord ye shall receive the reward of the inheritance: for ye serve the Lord Christ.” – Colossians 3:22-24. See also Psalm 2:11.

devotionals.theme: FRIENDSHIP OF THE WORLD IS ENMITY WITH GOD
devotionals.text: “Ye adulterers and adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? Whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God.” – James 4:4.
devotionals.comment: The word “friendship” is derived from the Greek word “philia” which denotes amity, fondness or liking. “World” refers to the vast number of people who have turned their backs on God, they take delight in executing the schemes of Satan the Devil – “the god of this world.” (2 Corinthians 4:4) “Enmity” means hostility or hatred. Put succinctly, it means all those who are disposed to things that are not in tandem with the will of God. It suffices to state that the Devil uses politics, religion and commerce to keep the world in his vile custody. (Luke 21:25,26) Those who misuse their privileges by resorting to dirty politics to trample upon the masses, those who are deceived by false religion and those greedy ones who want to purchase everything at their disposal will not be able to walk in harmony and in close relationship with God. (Hebrews 6:4-6; 10:26-27; James 4:4). Such ones should amend their ways by making friendship with God.

devotionals.theme: FRIENDSHIP OF THE WORLD IS ENMITY WITH GOD
devotionals.text: “Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the father is not in him...” – 1 John 2:15-17.
devotionals.comment: Man is a free moral agent. This being so, he has persisted in choosing causes that come far short of God's standards of loyalty or that are completely against His will. This is against the background of the fact that the Devil, conscious of man's pitfalls, entices him with sinful desires. These were the things the devil exploited in tempting Eve. She realised that “the tree was good for food” and that it was “pleasant to the eyes” and “a tree to be desired to make one wise”. This is an interplay of the lust of the flesh, eyes and pride of life (Genesis 3:5-7). By appealing to her fleshly lusts and pride, the Devil succeeded in getting to the man (Adam) to succumb to the woman's foolishness, not because he was deceived (1 Timothy 2:14) but because of his carnality which towered above his love for God. Thus, Adam and Eve were worldly and became estranged from God Almighty and the repercussions have been disastrous. – Genesis 3:16-19; Romans 5:12; 6:23.

devotionals.theme: FRIENDSHIP OF THE WORLD IS ENMITY WITH GOD
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “Children, obey your parents in the Lord for this is right. Honour, thy father and mother…That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.” – Ephesians 6:1-3.
devotionals.comment: Children of the kingdom should strive not to be detached from their spiritual tie. This is attainable through faith and obedience in the fear of God. King Solomon wrote: “A wise son heareth his father's instruction: but a scorner heareth not rebuke.” (Proverbs 13:1) A good child can be known by his subjection to his parents or guardian as was seen in Jesus Christ in his youth. (Luke 2:51) He must listen to instructions given by elders of the Church always. Students must pay attention to their studies and shun examination malpractices in any guise. Those who are married should be shining examples to others by living in love and harmony with their spouses. (Ephesians 5:21-25; Matthew 5:16). By clinging to these stern Christian principles, one is in friendship or harmony with God.

devotionals.theme: FRIENDSHIP OF THE WORLD IS ENMITY WITH GOD
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.” – Luke 16:9.
devotionals.comment: People of God should support the work of God by way of using their talents – spiritual, financial, physical, material, intellectual or otherwise. This will identify such ones as the friends of God and Christ and so earn true riches. We his disciples by God's grace should endeavour to make the Almighty God, the Father and His son Jesus Christ our friends by means of our material possessions, wealth or money so that in due course when things become difficult and money or worldly riches become things of the past (fail), “they may receive you into everlasting habitations.” (God's Kingdom) See Luke 16:9. We must give financial support to the work of God and further the cause of truth and righteousness by His grace. – Deuteronomy 8:11,12,17,18; 1 Chronicles 29:11,12.

devotionals.theme: FRIENDSHIP OF THE WORLD IS ENMITY WITH GOD
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “And Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him, and said to king Jehoshaphat, Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the LORD? Therefore is wrath upon thee from before the LORD.” – 2 Chronicles 19:1-3.
devotionals.comment:
Instances abound of people who while not violating the faith themselves, are not opposed to and do in fact support those who do so. One that quickly comes to mind is that of Jehoshaphat a king of Judah who was faithful to God but consented to help king Ahab in battle regardless of knowing the grave spiritual commitments of the king of Israel. But for God's mercy, Jehoshaphat would have been killed. On his return, God queried him for joining hands with Ahab to go to war: “Two cannot walk together except they be agreed”. (Amos 3:3) Jehoshaphat and Ahab were therefore strange bedfellows who should not be working together. (Romans 1:32).

The Holy Bible also enjoins us to come out from among them and be separate. (2 Corinthians 6:14-18) People of God should separate themselves from the things of this world that lead to destruction.

devotionals.theme: FRIENDSHIP OF THE WORLD IS ENMITY WITH GOD
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “And the LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend.” – Exodus 33:11.
devotionals.comment: The Prophet Moses is a classic example of one who distinguished himself by reason of his faithfulness to God. He was humble, gentle and peace-loving. But he abhorred oppression and injustice. Although, he was brought up as the son of Pharaoh's daughter, he prepared to “suffer affliction with the people of God than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.” (Hebrews 11:25) He was the instrument God used to deliver the children of Israel from the hands of Pharaoh. The greater challenge lay in enduring the stubbornness and backslidings of the people under his tutelage. On one occasion he stayed on Mount Sinai to receive the tablets of stone on which the laws of God were written. On his return, the people he was leading had turned their backs on God Almighty and he himself. But he maintained his unflinching loyalty to God. But for this godly quality of his, God would not have brought him close to Himself. No wonder St. Paul asserted: “But Moses verily was faithful in all his house, as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were to be spoken after.” – Hebrews 3:5.

devotionals.theme: FRIENDSHIP OF THE WORLD IS ENMITY WITH GOD
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “But now thy kingdom shall not continue: the LORD hath sought him a man after his own heart, and the LORD hath commanded him to be captain over his people, because thou hast not kept that which the LORD commanded thee.” – 1 Samuel 13:14.
devotionals.comment: David was a king in Israel and a prophet of God. Though of humble beginning, he was endowed with faith, courage and strength to the extent that he was able to kill a lion and a bear to protect his father's sheep. He displayed these qualities in his famous encounter with Goliath. While others were faint-hearted, he confronted Goliath with all courage and bravery and in the end, the LORD gave him victory. (1 Samuel 17). Even when King David offended God by engaging in adultery and murder, he chose the path of genuine repentance that God forgave him. (2 Samuel 12:1-23; 1 Kings 15:5) What is more, by reason of his faith, humility and sincerity, he is described in the Bible as a man after God's heart as seen in the text under review. – Acts 13:22.

devotionals.theme: FRIENDSHIP OF THE WORLD IS ENMITY WITH GOD
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “…For that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.” – Luke 16:15.
devotionals.comment: The opposite of friendship is enmity. It denotes the condition of being an enemy or mutual hostility. This is exhibited when one allows oneself to be seduced by the devil to tow the path of all that answers to unrighteousness. It is common place to see some youths taken through the terrain of evil by friends or age mates generally following the vogue of the age. This is dangerous as amplified by Christ in the text under focus. Youths should abstain from evil communications that corrupt good manners and must not follow a multitude to do evil. (1 Corinthians 15:33; Exodus 23:2) In the world today, many are engrossed with sinful pleasures and worldly lusts. (Colossians 3:5-10; 1 John 2:15-17) Those who are carried away with these vices will have themselves to blame at the end. (1 Corinthians 6:9,10; Galatians 5:19-21) People of God are warned. – Ephesians 5:6.

devotionals.theme: FRIENDSHIP OF THE WORLD IS ENMITY WITH GOD
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “Thus said the Lord, Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls. But they said, We will not walk therein.” – Jeremiah 6:16.
devotionals.comment: God Almighty is a God of order, and He is against all those who turn things upside down. (Isaiah 29:16) We must go back to the former days when reason or common sense, decency and orderliness informed the dress code for men and women. The vogue whereby women dress as men and some men dress as women is unacceptable, awkward, detestable to God, and very distant from the culture of decency. It ignites ungodliness and worldly lust and let confusion hold sway. It was God Almighty who declared through Prophet Jeremiah in the text under review. The level of permissiveness among youths in some developed countries today, is such that governments are helpless, and in their confusion, they are taking steps that compound the situation. For many women today, it is fashionable for them to wear trousers and put on clothes that expose their bodies. Some contend that there are female trousers. But research indicates that trousers are meant to be worn by men. The Holy Bible also supports this view. – Deuteronomy 22:5.

devotionals.theme: FRIENDSHIP OF THE WORLD IS ENMITY WITH GOD
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “The glory of young men is their strength...” – Proverbs 20:29.
devotionals.comment: Youths are restless and anxious to get things done quickly and are thus generally impatient. While these are virtues when used positively, they could also turn out to be monstrous vices if not controlled. Youths should not, in their quest for quick riches or easy solutions resort to violence, lie-telling, blackmail, kidnapping, stealing, arson, murder and so on. These are contrary to the laws of God. The Bible says: “The tabernacles of robbers prosper, and they that provoke God are secure…” (Job 12:6). The reason why many people commit acts of wickedness is that those who do such things are not always punished by God immediately. This was lucidly explained by Solomon in Ecclesiastes 8:11-13; Proverbs 5:22,23. Youths should endeavour to run away from these vices as they will not go unpunished at the end. – Job 20:4-9,20.

devotionals.theme: FRIENDSHIP OF THE WORLD IS ENMITY WITH GOD
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “…I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” – Matthew 9:10-13.
devotionals.comment:
If God is to kill everyone who sins against him immediately, not a single soul among the descendants of Adam will remain on earth because we are all sinners and it is in order to redeem us from sin Jesus Christ the righteous came to the world to give his life as a random. On this note, the Psalmist declared. “If thou LORD, shouldest mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand? But there is forgiveness with thee, that thou mayest be feared.” (Psalm 130:3,4) Everyone should take to honest labour and

practise righteousness to be prospered by the Most High. Youths who have been lured into errors of unrighteousness should turn a new leaf and show a genuine proof of repentance or contrition by serving God in truth. The door of salvation is still open to them. – Job 36:9-12; 2 Peter 3:9; Isaiah 1:18-20.

devotionals.theme: FRIENDSHIP OF THE WORLD IS ENMITY WITH GOD
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier. And if a man also strive for masteries, yet he is not crowned except he strive lawfully.” – 2 Timothy 2:4,5.
devotionals.comment: Timothy of Bible fame became a Christian from childhood. Besides the fact that it was St. Paul whom God used to bring him and his mother into the Christian faith, he responded positively to the training given him by St. Paul and so the learned apostle regarded him as his son in the Lord. He urged Timothy to be diligent in the study of the scriptures so as to be able to defend the faith aright. (2 Timothy 2:15) Moreover, he encouraged him to avoid “profane and vain babblings and oppositions of science falsely so-called which some professing have erred concerning the faith”. (1 Timothy 6:20,21) He further urged him to flee youthful lusts and to “follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart”. (2 Timothy 2:22) By so doing he would be an example to other believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.” (1 Timothy 4:12) He taught Timothy to endure hardness, that is to persevere in doing what is right even when things are rough, believing in the Lord's providence. – 2 Timothy 2:1-3.

devotionals.theme: FRIENDSHIP OF THE WORLD IS ENMITY WITH GOD
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?” – Mark 8:36,37.
devotionals.comment: Jesus Christ knew that because of the love some people have for money they are stingy and so find it hard to part with it even when its use for the work of God is an absolute necessity. But he wanted his disciples to realise that money or riches are carnal or temporal things. They come and go like a mirage or vanishing picture. On this note, King Solomon asserted: “Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? For riches certainly make themselves wings: they fly away as an eagle toward heaven.” (Proverbs 23:5) Over and above this, whatever money we are using now in this world would be useless in God's Kingdom when fully established on earth. The most anyone can make of his riches or money is to use it to the glory of God by contributing generously towards the furtherance of the saving gospel and by acts of charity towards the Ministers of God in particular and men of goodwill in general. – Galatians 6:10.

devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.” – Matthew 6:24.
devotionals.comment: It is common among some people of today, either because of the heat of devil's tribulations, they seek help from familiar spirits, witches and wizards. Anyone who engages in this act creates a vacuum between His Creator and himself. (1 Corinthians 10:21,22; Isaiah 30:1-3; 31:1-3) Those who obey the rules and regulations of secret societies and similar religious groups believing that they are serving God through those means are only living in a fool's paradise. We should not envy or follow them because their end will not be blessed unless they repent. St. Paul stated: “Be not ye therefore partakers with them. For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord: walk as children of light…And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness but rather reprove them.” (Ephesians 5:7-11; Psalm 37:35,36; Proverbs 23:17) Nothing should separate us from the love of Christ. – Romans 8:35-39.

devotionals.theme: FRIENDSHIP OF THE WORLD IS ENMITY WITH GOD
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “This know also, that in the last days, perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves...lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God.” – 2 Timothy 3:1,2,4.
devotionals.comment:
The fact is unarguable that many today give themselves to sinful pleasures without bothering how such indulgences affect their spiritual well-being. The prevalence of such attitudes is an indication that we are now in the last days. By so doing, they are making themselves enemies of God. While friendship with God and Christ will give us life and other attendant blessings, the opposite, though it may initially appear attractive, is unfruitful, culminating in sorrows, pain and death. To this end, James the apostle declared unequivocally: “Unfaithful people, don't you know that to be the world's friend means to be God's enemy? If you want to be the world's friend you make yourself God's enemy.” (James 4:4. Good News Bible) While making comments on the above text, Adam Clarke said: “it is strange that people professing Christianity can suppose that with a worldly spirit, worldly companions, and their lives governed by worldly maxims they can be in the favour of God.”

To be forewarned is to be forearmed. Our Lord and master admonished: “He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.” – Mark 4:9.

devotionals.theme: FIGHT THE GOOD FIGHT OF FAITH
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Before delving into the exhortation as captured in this theme, Paul the Apostle drew the attention of his son in the faith, young and zealous Timothy, concerning the danger of materialism, alerting him also of false teachers who saw materialism as godliness, and charged him on the virtue of contentment with godliness instead.  To fight the good fight of faith, therefore, entails resistance to all distractions or carnality, earnestly contending for the faith, and prioritising God's Kingdom interest, by the grace of God.
devotionals.text: “But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you.” – Matthew 6:33.
devotionals.comment: Scriptural understanding furnishes us with an indepth appreciation of the concept of “selflessness” in the course of our worship to our Maker, even if it means foregoing personal comfort, resources, energy, time, etc. During his earthly ministry, “a certain man said unto him, Lord, I will follow thee withersoever thou goest. And Jesus said unto him, Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head. And he said to another, follow me. But he said, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father…” (Luke 9:57-61) Genuine conversion to the true faith thus implies wholesome dedication to matters of the kingdom, without consideration for personal schedule, adamic ties, etc., and continuing on this path, till the end, in that, “No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.” – Luke 9:62.

devotionals.text: “Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” – James 4:7
devotionals.comment: It requires God's help for one to effectively “fight the good fight of faith”. (Psalm 60:12; 108:13) On our part, we should realise that He, the Almighty Father would only give us the spiritual enablement, when we give ourselves to Him. “Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” (James 4:8) As we know, our affinity to, or admiration for sinful pleasures, presents the devil with the ability to weaken our faith. Having enumerated sundry qualities to aid Christians in the fight of faith, Apostle Peter added: “But he that lacketh these things is blind, and cannot see afar off, and hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins.” (2 Peter 1:9) Because sin compromises the effectiveness of the spiritual “shield”, “breastplate”, “sword”, “helmet”, etc., the Holy Bible exhorts: “If iniquity be in thine hand, put it far away, and let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacles.” – Ephesians 6:11-17; Job 11:14.

devotionals.text: “Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints.” – Jude vs 3
devotionals.comment:
Christ had earlier intimated Christian converts of the relevance of the knowledge of God, with respect to salvation in John 17:3. Concerning this knowledge of the truth, Paul the apostle wrote: “For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: For it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.” (Romans 1:16) Naturally, one cannot give what he does not have. This amplifies the importance of knowledge, which the Preacher refers to as a “defence”, (Ecclesiastes 7:12) and “sword of the Spirit” by St. Paul, in Ephesians 6:17; Hebrews 4:12.

God helping us, with the fortification we get from the gospel of peace, and a host of other requirements in the “whole armour of God,” we would be able to “stand against the wiles of the devil”, and to “exhort and to convince the gainsayers…” – Ephesians 6:11; Titus 1:9-11.

devotionals.text: “For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh: (For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds)” – 2 Corinthians 10:3,4.
devotionals.comment: It was Paul, an apostle of Christ, who charged Timothy, to wit: “Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God. (2 Timothy 1:8) Following the miraculous healing on the lame man at the gate of the temple, the duo of Peter and John faced persecutions from the Sanhedrin, the judicial council of the Jews, because of the growing popularity of the Christian faith. In response to the warning, prohibiting them from preaching in Christ's name, they retorted: “whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye. For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard.” When asked to defend themselves, the apostles replied: “We ought to obey God rather than men.” After they had been beaten, the account has it that: “And they departed from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for his name.” (Acts chapters 3; 4 and 5) This is highly commendable, and worth emulating.

devotionals.text: “And what shall I more say? For the time would fail me to tell of Gedeon, and of Barak, and of Samson, and of Jephthae; of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets: who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions.” – Hebrews 11:32,33.
devotionals.comment: In the infinitude of His mercies, God Almighty bestowed on us, His attribute of power, is one evidence of His likeness in us, for us to, among other reasons, perform exploits, under the direction of His Holy Spirit, where we are not faithless. The inclusion of David to the heroes of fame and of faith, brings to mind, his defeat of Goliath, whom he had earlier described as an uncircumcised Philistine.” (1 Samuel 17:26,36) The Giant of Gath, measuring six cubits and a span whose size as the Living Bible states: “He was a giant of a man measuring over nine feet tall.” He had been making blasphemous remarks against the Most High, and the people of God, long before David's arrival, yet none of the Israelites were courageous enough to confront him, “all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him, and were sore afraid” (verse 24). When worshippers of God can imbibe the fear of God, He in turn would use them mightily by His grace. In our quest to excel in the fight of faith, we should endeavour to have faith in our Maker, without which, none can please Him. – Hebrews 11:6.

devotionals.text: “By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter; choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season; Esteeming the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures in Egypt: for he had respect unto the recompence of the reward.” – Hebrews 11:24-26.
devotionals.comment: In Moses, we learn of uncommon patriotism and love for God, and the Israel of old, his fellow compatriots. It is on record that the name, “Moses”, was given to him by Pharaoh's daughter. (Exodus 2:10) Yet, Moses forsook the pleasures of Egyptian royalty, and chose to identify with the sufferings of the people of God, similar to our Lord Jesus Christ, the “Greater Moses”, “…though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich.” (2 Corinthians 8:9) To effectively fight the good fight of faith, we must be humble, (1 Peter 5:5) ready to suffer inconveniences for the gospel's sake (Philippians 4:11,12) and set our focus on the promised prize always. – Hebrews 11:9; 10,38,39; 12:2.

devotionals.comment: While running the race of salvation, there comes a time when we must deliberately take certain drastic decisions for the good of all, not minding whose ox is gored! At a time of national crisis, by way of plague, brought about by Israel's descent to immorality and idolatry, “one of the children of Israel came and brought unto his brethren a Midianitish woman in the sight of Moses, and in the sight of all the congregation.” On seeing this act of impunity, Phinehas, Aaron's grandson, took a javelin and “went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her belly. So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel.” (Numbers 25:1-8) This act of bravery and zeal, earned him God's approval, commendation and blessing, among which was the “covenant of an everlasting priesthood” by God's grace. – Numbers 25:10-13; Galatians 4:18.

devotionals.text: “Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry: for which things' sake the wrath of God cometh on the children of disobedience.” – Colossians 3:5,6.
devotionals.comment:
There must be evidence of spiritual progress, while we are striving to be saved. Such measurable progress, brings about inner satisfaction, a feeling of accomplishment, and an encouragement to make further gains, by the grace of God. We cannot claim to be working out our salvation, when we are glued to the “old man”.

Where this is the case, then we are not being diligent to make our election sure, God forbid. Writing on the unfortunate relapse to godlessness by the Galatian converts, Paul the Apostle lamented: “Howbeit then, when ye knew not God, ye did service unto them which by nature are no gods.

But now, after that ye have known God, or rather are known of God, how turn ye again to the weak and beggarly elements, whereunto ye desire again to be in bondage...I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain.” (Galatians 4:8-11) Fighting the good fight of faith, being a continuous process, requires persistent effort, till perfection is attained, by the grace of God.

devotionals.text: “Wherefore do ye spend money for that which is not bread? And your labour for that which satisfieth not? Hearken diligently unto me, and eat ye that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness.” – Isaiah 55:2.
devotionals.comment: The Holy Bible is consistent in pointing out that not all services are accepted by God Almighty. For our services to be accepted, they must be in the way of truth. (Ezekiel 20:40; John 4:23,24) It therefore follows that, services rendered outside God's mountain, amount to mere vanity fair. As such, we should endeavour to remain in her, steadfastly unto the end, God willing. On no account should we allow offences, trials, or our own negligence by way of distractions, make us return to “Egypt”, having “tasted of the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come.” The implication of backsliding is, in addition to crucifying “the son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame”, such ones end up making a shipwreck of their faith. (Hebrews 6:4-6; 1 Timothy 1:19) Concerning the potency of the truth in sustaining God's children in the quest for life eternal, the Psalmist wrote: “Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” – Psalm 119:165.

devotionals.text: “For unto you it is given in the behalf of Christ, not only to believe on him, but also to suffer for his sake.” – Philippians 1:29.
devotionals.comment:
No one of God's worshippers was ever promised a rosy ride to the finishing line, “For verily, when we were with you, we told you before that we should suffer tribulation; even as it came to pass, and ye know.” (1 Thessalonians 3:4; Acts 14;22) Thus, one evidence of true discipleship is, preparedness to suffer for the sake of Christ.

Ordinarily, the term “fight of faith” as used in the theme, is already suggestive of combating the forces of evil (2 Corinthains 10:4,5) and battling to subdue or conquer besetting sins, to “run with patience the race that is set before us”. (Hebrews 12:1) With the above understanding, “Though the way be dreary, while the foes array, yet, by Jesus's power we tread without fear…with this hope of freedom, Go we in Thy name, joyfully and boldly, with songs of victory.”

devotionals.text: “And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible.” – 1 Corinthians 9:25.
devotionals.comment:
One is justifiably adjudged to be “temperate” when one exhibits modesty in the indulgence of his natural appetites or passions. In this regard, the erudite Apostle educates believers using a personal approach he adopted, “But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.” (verse 27) Owing to Satan's active influence, the daily struggle to conquer easily besetting sins, gaining control over our fleshly desires, ability to prioritise God's Kingdom interests over personal pursuits, etc, all require self-discipline, and God's grace ultimately.

Eternal life being the end result, we are encouraged that no sin is too pleasurable or life pursuit so rewarding to the detriment of eternal bliss, peace, prosperity, etc., in the fully established kingdom of God. – Romans 8:13; Hebrews 12:1; Colossians 3:5.

devotionals.text: “Labour not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life, which the son of man shall give unto you: for him hath God the Father sealed.” – John 6:27.
devotionals.comment: In his detailed analysis on the emptiness of a world under the control of our chief adversary, Satan the Devil, the “god of this world” the Preacher uses the noun “vanity” over thirty times, all through the Book of Ecclesiastes. This is suggestive of the great loss awaiting all who aspire for vainglory, setting aside Theocratic causes, for personal gratification. “For he that soweth to his flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he that soweth to the spirit shall of the spirit reap life everlasting.” (Galatians 6:8) Christ's exhortation in verse 27 of John chapter six, is in reaction to the frantic effort made by some persons who went in search of him, following the miraculous feeding of 5,000 persons with five loaves of bread, and two small fishes. Our efforts should rather be in pursuit of things spiritual, as against carnality. “Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.” – Hebrews 4:11.

devotionals.text: “And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.” – Luke 12:15.
devotionals.comment: Our redeemer, Jesus Christ, had earlier asked: “For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?” (Mark 8:36) It is appalling, seeing the extent people are ready to go to “make a statement” by way of proving that they have “arrived”. “Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!” (Isaiah 5:8) One who is pre-occupied with such target, may find it difficult to meet his spiritual obligations, often giving excuses, or having one “project” or the other to undertake. It was the godly disposition of the centurion, coupled with faith in God, that earned him commendation from the elders of the Jews, to Jesus Christ, to wit: “And when they came to Jesus, they besought him instantly, saying, that he was worthy for whom he should do this: For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue.” – Luke 7:4,5; Romans 8:5,6.

devotionals.theme: FIGHT THE GOOD FIGHT OF FAITH
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Before delving into the exhortation as captured in this theme, Paul the Apostle drew the attention of his son in the faith, young and zealous Timothy, concerning the danger of materialism, alerting him also of false teachers who saw materialism as godliness, and charged him on the virtue of contentment with godliness instead.  To fight the good fight of faith, therefore, entails resistance to all distractions or carnality, earnestly contending for the faith, and prioritising God's Kingdom interest, by the grace of God.
devotionals.text: “Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.” – Philippians 3:13,14.
devotionals.comment: The All-wise God who searches the heart, and tries the reins, “is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” (Jeremiah 17:10; 1 Samuel 2:3) At no time should we, as candidates of salvation”, allow the Devil instil in us, a feeling of infallibility (1 Corinthians 10:12) or that we have done enough, in the cause of fighting the good fight of faith, forgetting that, our righteousness at best, are as “filthy rags”. (Isaiah 64:6) Notwithstanding, his noble contributions by way of missionary journeys, partaking in Christ's sufferings, authorship of no less than 13 Books of the Holy Bible, etc., Paul the apostle stated that he did not see himself as one who had attained anything. This is most instructive, especially coming from an apostle of Jesus Christ. For us therefore, we should continue to “Fight on while the Foe is unconquered yet: no laying of the armour down: no fainting till battle's vantage we get, and vict'ry wins for us “ternal life” by the grace of God.

To fight the good fight of faith, therefore, entails resistance to all distractions or carnality, earnestly contending for the faith, and prioritising God's Kingdom interest, by the grace of God.
devotionals.text: “Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.” – Hebrews 12:2.
devotionals.comment: Christ Jesus our Chief Exemplar, by precept and example, laid for us, standard on how to successfully fight the good fight of faith not minding the “contradiction of sinners against himself”, he endured the humiliation, despise, rejection, etc, and today, has gained justification in Mount Zion above. Like his Master, Jesus Christ, St. Paul considered all of his accomplishments prior to his conversion, as loss: “But what things were gain to me, those I counted loss for Christ. Yea doubtless, and I count all things but loss for the excelling of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and do count them but dung, that I may win Christ”. (Philippians 3:7,8) The reward for prioritising the quest for life everlasting is sure. “To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life.” – Romans 2:7.

devotionals.theme: DOING THE WILL OF GOD FROM THE HEART
devotionals.text: “Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled.” – Titus 1:15.
devotionals.comment:
In this journey of faith, the purification of one's heart begins when one answers the call of God by accepting the gospel of truth that washes and cleanses one from sin. “Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.” (John 15:3; 17:17) As followers of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart, sincerity and uprightness cannot be over emphasised. When a man serves God with a willing mind and a perfect heart or “a conscience void of offence toward God and towards men.” (Acts 24:16) He tends to understand spiritual things easily, clearly and within a good time.

But to those who are wicked and defiled, it is not so. As Apostle Paul stated in the leading text: “Everything is pure to those whose hearts are pure. But nothing is pure to those who are corrupt and unbelieving, because their minds and consciences are defiled. Such people claim they know God, but they deny Him by the way they live. They are rotten and disobedient, worthless for doing anything good.” – Titus 1:15, 16. (The Living Bible).

devotionals.theme: DOING THE WILL OF GOD FROM THE HEART
devotionals.text: “And thou, Solomon my son, know thou the God of thy father, and serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind: for the LORD searcheth all hearts, and understandeth all the imaginations of the thoughts: if thou seek him, he will be found of thee; but if thou forsake him, he will cast thee off for ever.” – 1 Chronicles 28:9.
devotionals.comment: King David, the Sweet Psalmist of Israel, served God with an upright heart and a willing mind. God referred to him as “a man after my own heart” (1 Samuel 13:14; Acts 13:22) When he committed adultery with Bathsheba, Uriah's wife and murdering her husband, Nathan the prophet called his attention to it. He did not justify himself as King but showed sincere repentance from the heart. God Almighty forgave him. (2 Samuel 12:1-15) In his prayer, King David declared: “Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me. Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.” (Psalm 51:10,11) This was why he charged his son, Solomon to serve God with “a perfect heart and with a willing mind.” For God “renderest to every man according to his work.” (Psalm 62:12) “I the LORD search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doing.” – Jeremiah 17:10.

devotionals.theme: DOING THE WILL OF GOD FROM THE HEART
devotionals.text: “And now, behold, the LORD hath kept me alive, as He said, these forty and five years, even since the LORD spake this word unto Moses, while the children of Israel wandered in the wilderness; and now, lo, I am this day fourscore and five years old.” – Joshua 14:10.
devotionals.comment:
God's love, strength and protections are not limited to the heroes of faith in the Bible, who did the will of God from the heart. These blessings are also available to everyone who is willing to do same in this age irrespective of our colours and languages.

When duties are assigned to us and we carry them out willingly and wholeheartedly, as leaders, servants or workers, we open ourselves up to receive God's blessings and guidance, just as Caleb. Moses the Prophet in his days, assigned to Caleb and other eleven men the duty to spy the land of Canaan. (Numbers 13:1-17) It was only Joshua and Caleb that carried out the duty assigned to them with willingness and sincerity of heart.

In the leading text for today, Caleb was now recounting the goodness and mercies of God towards him for his good works. (Joshua 14:10, 11) Obviously, God's blessings await those who do the work “not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart.” – Ephesians 6:6.

devotionals.theme: DOING THE WILL OF GOD FROM THE HEART
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the LORD. And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the LORD had respect unto Abel and to his offering.” – Genesis 4:3,4.
devotionals.comment: Our actions and words sometime picture what we have in mind and what we can do, just as it is said “actions speak louder than words.” The man Abel willingly gave the best of all he had to God, and God accepted his sacrifices. (Genesis 4:4) “Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.” (2 Corinthians 9:7) But Cain in his mind thought he could deceive God by just doing it the way he wants and not doing it right, just as some persons do today, forgetting that God sees the heart. “Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap. And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.” – Galatians 6:7,9; Jeremiah 17:10.

devotionals.theme: DOING THE WILL OF GOD FROM THE HEART
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.” – Psalm 139:23,24.
devotionals.comment: When one carries out the duty or duties assigned to him, with sincerity and uprightness of heart, in the fear of God and without fear or favour, he fears no accusation, criticism or the receiving of corrections. This was why Samuel the Prophet in his days declared; “Behold, here I am: witness against me before the LORD, and before his anointed: whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I received any bribe to blind mine eyes therewith? and I will restore it you. And they said, Thou hast not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither hast thou taken ought of any man's hand.” (1 Samuel 12:3,4) As believers, it is vital we note that God's word is a hidden treasure waiting to be discovered in the depths of our hearts when we continue to internalise and practise them. May God search and create in us a clean heart and a renewed spirit to continue to do His will from the heart by His grace. Amen. – Psalm 51:10.

devotionals.theme: DOING THE WILL OF GOD FROM THE HEART
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.” – Matthew 15:8,9.
devotionals.comment:
As Christians we need not become discouraged or complacent in our pursuit of seeking God. Rather, let us have a burning desire within us to seek Him with all our heart and soul. When we do so, we will discover the richness of His presence and the abundance of His grace that will attract His blessings. But any activity with eye service, with the intent to please men and not God, and without sincere and faithful worship from the heart is hypocrisy. Our worship to God Almighty should be void of hypocrisy. There are some who harbour malice, hatred and envy in their hearts but do put up a broad smile when they see their fellow brother or sister.

This is not good.

We should take note that God Almighty sees our hearts and there is nothing that can be hidden from Him. – Matthew 15:7-9; Mark 7:6; Isaiah 29:13.

devotionals.theme: DOING THE WILL OF GOD FROM THE HEART
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “And the LORD said unto David my father, Whereas it was in thine heart to build an house unto my name, thou didst well that it was in thine heart.” – 1 Kings 8:18.
devotionals.comment: When we fill our heart with the word of God, by meditating on it, it serves as a guiding light, permeating our thoughts and attitudes, illuminating our paths and guarding us from the pitfalls of this world. King David in his days thought of building a permanent place of worship, a befitting house for the name of the LORD God of Israel, where the Ark of the LORD would be kept. This good thought from King David was well pleasing in the sight of God. For this, God made rich promises to David, to his sons and to his generations to come. (2 Samuel 7:2-17) This goes to show that when one has a good heart and a willing mind towards God and the progress of His work, He is pleased and will always bless such a person by His grace and power. – Hebrews 6:10; Psalm 37:25; 2 Samuel 7:19,20.

devotionals.theme: DOING THE WILL OF GOD FROM THE HEART
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “And whatever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord and not unto men. Knowing that of the Lord ye shall receive the reward of the inheritance: for ye serve the Lord Christ.” – Colossians 3:23,24.
devotionals.comment: God is aware of every detail and even the seemingly insignificant tasks we do. Our little acts of kindness, our humble and sincere service behind the scenes, He sees them all and will always reward us. Having a good heart and a willing mind in following Christ, keeping His commandment, helps in activating good thought and actions in the way of truth and righteousness. Christ stated: “A good tree can't produce bad fruit, and bad tree can't produce good fruit. A tree is identified by the kind of fruit it produces. Figs never grow on thorn bushes or grapes on bramble bushes. A good person produces good deeds from a good heart, and an evil person produces evil deeds from an evil heart. Whatever is in your heart determines what you say.” – Luke 6:43-45 (Living Bible). See also Matthew 12:33-35.

devotionals.theme: DOING THE WILL OF GOD FROM THE HEART
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “Therefore also now, saith the LORD, turn ye even to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning. And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the LORD your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.” – Joel 2:12,13.
devotionals.comment:
In the service of God, some worshippers believe that mere fasting, praying, weeping and mourning to show remorse is enough to please Him. But it is by far more than what they think.

God Almighty sees our hearts hence; He desires thorough repentance from the innermost heart, not pretence. King Solomon says God weighs the heart and assesses our motives. (Proverbs 16:2; 21:2) In today's text, Joel the prophet called on the people to rent their hearts and not their garments. This reminds us that true repentance and turning to God requires a deep inner transformation. “Rending our hearts” means giving, yielding and surrendering ourselves completely to the will of God. Let us allow God to mould our character towards holiness and to use us as fitting vessels in His service. We should totally and truly concede our hearts to God Almighty and endeavour to always do His will to receive His manifold blessings at the end by His grace and power.

devotionals.theme: DOING THE WILL OF GOD FROM THE HEART
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “And now, Israel, what doth the LORD thy God require of thee, but to fear the LORD thy God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve the LORD thy God with all thy heart and with all thy soul.” – Deuteronomy 10:12.
devotionals.comment: The laws and commandments of God are also known as “the word of life,” “the sword of the spirit” (Philippians 2:16; Ephesians 6:17.) When we read and obey the laws of God, it gives one wisdom and intelligence. It helps in cleansing us of our sins, guiding and directing our ways of life for one's benefit always. It is important to serve God Almighty with our utmost and with all He has blessed us with. “And the LORD commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the LORD our God, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive, as it is at this day. And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the LORD our God, as he hath commanded us.” – Deuteronomy 6:24,25. Also read Psalm 119:9,11; John 15:3.

devotionals.theme: DOING THE WILL OF GOD FROM THE HEART
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “But the LORD said unto Samuel, look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the LORD seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.”  – 1 Samuel 16:7.
devotionals.comment:
The heart of man is deceitful and wicked. It is only God that sees the thoughts and understands the imaginations of the hearts of men.

(Jeremiah 17:9,10) Serving God is not all about outward appearance which sometimes is deceptive, but good attitude and total commitment with sincerity of the heart and mind. One may be doing what is considered good and just before men, but with selfish and ulterior motive. Just as Amaziah did in his days, for he did what was right in the sight of God “but not with a perfect heart.” (2 Chronicles 25:1,2) God looks or sees beyond man's imaginations and thoughts, as showed in the text for today. God speaking through Isaiah the prophet stated: “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways…For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.” – Isaiah 55:8,9.

devotionals.theme: DOING THE WILL OF GOD FROM THE HEART
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man. For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies. These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man.” – Matthew 15:18-20.
devotionals.comment: The keeping of our hearts or our deep thoughts away from all forms of evil, especially in the last days where there are lots of distractions from social media, betting, sports, fashion, customs and traditions cannot be over-emphasised. The Scribes and Pharisees came to Jesus Christ condemning his disciples for not washing their hands before eating bread. The answer that Christ gave them was that what defiles a person is not eating with unwashed hands or the kind of food a person eats, but the thoughts and actions coming from his heart. (Matthew 15:1-20) “Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.” (Proverbs 4:23) Our Lord and Master Jesus Christ further stated: “…You take care to seem right in the eyes of men, but God sees your hearts: and those things which are important in the opinion of men, are evil in the eyes of God...” – Luke 16:15 (Bible in Basic English).

devotionals.theme: DOING THE WILL OF GOD FROM THE HEART
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.” – Matthew 6:33.
devotionals.comment: Seeking God first and His righteousness requires our wholehearted devotion and commitment in all we do and speak. It means putting God first in all we do and turning away from all worldly distractions and ungodly desires that are against the will and commandment of God. As humans, sometimes in life, we go through ups and downs. There are moments when we may feel overwhelmed and incapable of finding a way out of the difficult situation we find ourselves. But when our hearts and minds are rooted in the word of God, the way of truth, by seeking His righteousness, He, according to His promises, will see us through and will answer all our prayers and “all these things shall be added unto you.” – Psalm 145:18,19; Matthew 6:33.

devotionals.theme: DOING THE WILL OF GOD FROM THE HEART
devotionals.themeIntroduction: Continued from the last issue
devotionals.text: “Amaziah was twenty and five years old when he began to reign… And he did that which was right in the sight of God, but not with a perfect heart.” – 2 Chronicles 25:1,2.
devotionals.comment: Man, sometimes can deceive himself and those around him for a while, but can never at any time deceive God. For the Lord searches the hearts of men and try the reins, and giveth to every man according to his ways and the fruits of his doings. (Jeremiah 17:10) In the service of God, it is important to understand that insincerity like eye service and lip service have no blessing or reward from God. Just like the case of Amaziah who did “what was right in the sight of God but not with a perfect heart.” (2 Chronicles 25:2) This was why Apostle Paul in his charge to the Christians in Ephesus stated: “Not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart; With good will doing service, as to the Lord, and not to men: knowing that whatsoever good thing any man doeth, the same shall he received of the Lord, whether he be bond or free.” – Ephesians 6:6-8.

devotionals.theme: COME OUT FROM AMONG THEM AND BE YE SEPARATE
devotionals.themeIntroduction: The phrase, “come out from among them” originates from the statement of Apostle Paul where he urges Christians to separate themselves from ungodly influences. It emphasises the need for believers to maintain a distinct identity and not be yoked with unbelievers. As true Christians who have come to know the truth, right conduct or behaviour is expected of us. We are expected to discontinue or cut off our association with persons who are not morally upright and those who are opposed to truth and righteousness so as not to suffer the spiritual consequences that will befall such ungodly persons in the end. – Isaiah 52:11.
devotionals.text: “Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? And what communion hath light with darkness?” – 2 Corinthians 6:14.
devotionals.comment: St. Paul admonished true Christians not to team up with or join unbelievers in their activities because there is no fellowship between righteousness and unrighteousness, and there is no communion between light and darkness. Though many people in the world love darkness, that is, engage in ungodly practices (John 3:19), true worshippers of God are expected to be of exemplary conduct, standing up for the truth and God's righteousness wherever they found themselves. Notable examples are those of Lot in Sodom, who maintained his integrity (2 Peter 2:6-8) and the three faithful Jews, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, whose blunt refusal to worship King Nebuchadnezzar's golden image led to miraculous scenes which compelled the King to make a decree that no other God should be worshipped in his kingdom save the Living God. (Daniel 3:1–30) As serious Christians, we are not to flounder in any spiritually-committing association with unbelievers who are still wallowing in ignorance about the purpose of God. See Matthew 5:16; 6:24; 1 Corinthians 10:20,21; Philippians 2:15.

devotionals.text: “Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” – 1 Corinthians 15:33.
devotionals.comment: A good Christian character could be corrupted in a person who keeps company with ungodly people. This is so because intimacy with bad principles or behaviour, over time, definitely dilutes one's own thinking and character. Peer group influence and a desire to “keep up with the Joneses” are destructive allurements to the youths. There is a well-known adage which says: “Tell me who your friends are, and I will tell you who you are.” This is usually prevalent with young and inexperienced minds – the youths. Through wrong association, some youths have involved themselves in certain criminal acts which land them in serious, inextricable trouble, while some have had to cut short their educational pursuits, business models, foreign trips with expectant hopes for an enhanced life. To avoid these pitfalls, true Christians should carefully choose the company they keep, stick with God-fearing ones, who heed godly counsel by the grace of God. Read Matthew 10:16; Psalm 19:7-11; Proverbs 6:23.

devotionals.text: “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.” – Psalm 1:1.
devotionals.comment: King David, the Sweet Psalmist of Israel begins the Psalms by extolling the blessedness and joy of obeying God's commandments and dissociating oneself from the company of jesters and scorners. For the spiritually unwary, their friends and associates can have profound influence on them, often in subtle ways, when they walk by the advice they offer. If we become friends with those who mock or ridicule spiritual matters, we might fall into sin by becoming indifferent to ungodly principles. God forbid. King David lamented: “They blaspheme your name…O LORD, shouldn't I hate those who hate you? Shouldn't I be grieved with them? Yes, I hate them, for your enemies are my enemies too.” (Psalm 139:20-22) – The Living Bible. The ungodly are deceitful and selfish. They have no principles. We should learn from the episode between Ahab, the idol worshipper and Jehoshaphat, the King of Judah as recorded in 2 Chronicles 19:1-10.

devotionals.text: “And what concord hath Christ with Belial? Or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?” – 2 Corinthians 6:15.
devotionals.comment: The text for today is a rhetorical question, stressing the fact that our Lord Jesus Christ can never ever have any connection with Belial (Satan). Likewise, will a true believer not compromise his faith with an unbeliever. There is no concord or common ground between a convert and an infidel since they will not agree on matters of faith. The prophet of God, Amos asked a pertinent question, “Can two walk together, except they be agreed?” (Amos 3:3) Compare Luke 16:13. St. Paul charged Christian believers, thus “Ye cannot drink the cup of the Lord, and the cup of devils, ye cannot be partakers of the Lord's table, and of the table of devils.” (1 Corinthians 10:21. See also Matthew 4:10; John 14:30,31) As honest worshippers of God, we should not associate with red-herring activities inspired by Satan the Devil, no matter how glamorous they may appear. We should be wary of his deceit to making a potentially dangerous situation less serious. Apostle Paul says: “Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” – 2 Corinthians 2:11.

devotionals.text: “And what agreement hath the temple of God with idols?” – 2 Corinthians 6:16.
devotionals.comment:
It is quite unfortunate and disheartening that up till today, people still make idols and worship them, the works of their own hands, leaving the only true God, JEHOVAH, Who dwells in the Heaven of heavens. (Psalm 11:4; 48:2; 115:2,3).

Idolatry is an abomination to God. It is a mark of foolishness and stupidity for people to leave the true God to serve objects. These idols “have mouths but cannot speak, they have ears but cannot hear; they smell not with their noses; they have hands but cannot handle, feet have they, but cannot walk…” (Psalm 115:4-8) God Almighty abhors the worship of idols. He instructed the Jews in the Decalogue, “Thou shall not make unto thee any graven image… thou shall not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them” (Exodus 20: 4,5) For us who have come to the knowledge of the truth, it would be highly sacrilegious to abandon the way of holiness to serve idols. St. Peter says, “For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness...” – 2 Peter 2:21.

devotionals.text: “For the time past of our life may suffice us to have wrought the will of the Gentiles, when we walked in lasciviousness, lust, excess of wine, revellings, banqueting, and abominable idolatries.” – 1 Peter 4:3.
devotionals.comment: Being humans, we might have been involved in unwholesome activities in the past when we had not been truly converted or were still low in knowledge and understanding of the word of God. At that time, some of us spent our time, to use the words of Apostle Paul, “in rioting and drunkenness, in chambering and wantonness, in strife and envying” (Romans 13:13; See also Acts 17:30,31) Our embrace of the truth has positioned us for God's blessings and salvation, on the condition that we do not “build again those things” which we have destroyed. (Galatians 2:18) Instead, as the apostle of Christ admonished, we should: “put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof.” (Romans 13:14) In this age of the acceptable year of the Lord, the door is still open for repentance and to “be born again” as new creatures. This is crucial if not one “cannot see the kingdom of God”. (John 3:3; Ephesians 4:24; 1 Peter 2:11) We should pray for more faith and understanding to continue in the way of holiness until the end. – See Isaiah 35:8.

devotionals.comment: Sin is enticing. It could give some people a sense of gain or advantage. It sometimes emboldens one to use short cuts to achieving their goals. Such thinking is a quick means to false and deceptive prosperity. “Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant” (Proverbs 9:17) This means that “forbidden actions feel exciting, thrilling, or “sweeter” simply because they are illicit…leading ultimately to death, destruction, and regret.” There are people who were calm, humble and easy-going, but when they assume positions of authority, their visage, thinking and manner of speech changed into near tyranny. They become conscious of their ego, office, prestige rather than “walk the work”. The God of Israel, the Rock of Israel, the Almighty God says, “He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God.” (2 Samuel 23:3) As true Christians our focus should be on how to imitate the good and keep away from following those who indulge in evil practices. See Romans 6:23; James 1:14,15; Matthew 5:45.
